item.title: Kobe's Covered Shopping Arcades: Local Life Under the Roof — Guide
item.description: Behind Kobe’s glossy department stores runs a very different city: long covered shotengai arcades where the shutters are old, the lighting is fluorescent and the shops have been in the same families for generations. Stretching for blocks between Motomachi and Sannomiya and on toward Shinkaichi, they mix greengrocers and fishmongers with secondhand record shops, tiny standing bars, cheap noodle counters and Showa-era cafes. It’s the antidote to the tourist waterfront — cheap, rainproof and full of everyday life, and among the most enjoyable ways to see how Kobe actually lives.
